Commentary.Commentary: Conditions have become slightly overcast. Perfect for Jimmy the master. Tom Latham and Devon Conway are the openers for New Zealand. It will be James Anderson to Tom Latham first up...
... SECOND INNINGS...
Right then. Is 303 good enough? We shall know. The players are back on the field.

New Zealand would be disappointed. They had England on the ropes but allowed the home side to get away. Boult and Henry shared 7 wickets amongst themselves but Wagner was a disappointment. Ajaz Patel did well.

England actually started off well with the bat but then, had a collapse, as usual. Rory Burns tried hanging around, approaching another century but New Zealand kept chipping away on Thursday afternoon. It was then that the hosts found an unlikely hero in Dan Lawrence. His splendid unbeaten 81 definitely gave them control but one cannot ignore the contributions of Olly Stone and Mark Wood. Stone made 20 in a stand of 47 for the 7th wicket while Wood enjoyed himself, making 41 in a partnership of 66. His innings this morning gave England a massive lift.

Well, no century for Dan Lawrence but England have got a competitve score. It is a really good recovery from 175/6. 128 runs for the last 4 wickets, with Lawrence making 55 of those. So you can see the contribution of the other players. Fantastic from the lower order.

OUT! LBW! What a review by Latham! At the last-minute! Ross Taylor did not seem too excited at first slip but Boult was and Latham went with his bowler. Full, outside off, nipping back in, James Anderson looked to drive but missed. He got hit on the pads and initial reaction was a inside edge. Umpire Richard Kettleborough shook his head and Boult demanded a review from his skipper. Latham looked at Rosco who did not seem to be too sure but the review was taken. The inside edge got checked first but UltraEdge detected no inside edge. Next was the Ball Tracker which showed three reds, with the ball hitting the leg stump! Boult gets 4 and ENGLAND FINISH ON 303.
Outside off, moving away, a play and a miss. That is 5 balls survived in this over.
On a length, around off, nudged towards short mid-wicket.
Full and straight, watchfully defended. Very well played. That was swinging but he watched the ball till the last moment. Boult smiles and Jimmy smiles back in response. Good to see.
On a length, just outside off, Anderson looks to push and gets an outside edge, which goes on the ground to third slip.
Full, outside off, James Anderson looks to drive but misses.
Backs away to the leg side again but this time, Wagner follows him. Dan looks to flick but misses and the ball goes between his legs, to the keeper.
FOUR! 300 UP FOR ENGLAND. Full, outside off, Lawrence moves back and flays it over cover. Moves to 81 now.
Outside off, whipped to mid-wicket. No run taken.
Outside off, Dan looks to play the upper cut but misses.

Possible return catch! But that went in a flash. Full, around off, Lawrence walks across and hits it straight back, uppishly. Neil Wagner looks to catch but by the time his left hand comes up, the ball is through and past him. Matt Henry does really well to race to his left from long on and dive, pushing the ball away. Two runs taken. The stand moves to 10.
A length ball, around middle, Dan Lawrence comes down the track and swings hard, but mistimes it towards mid on.
Here comes the short-ball specialist. Neil Wagner comes on to try and finish this innings off. 20-6-62-1 so far.
Full and wide outside off, JA looks to drive (but why?) and misses.
Around off, pushed towards gully.
A shorter ball, around off, angling away, Jimmy sways away.
Down the leg side, Anderson misses his flick.
Change in field. Leg slip comes out and moves to gully.
FOUR! Useful runs. Outside off, moving away, James Anderson just opens the face of his bat and guides it past second slip, to the third man fence.
Short ball, around middle, nudged away.
Full, on the pads, cannot get it past mid-wicket even with a flick.
FOUR! Nicely played. Full, outside off, Dan Lawrence backs away and lofts it over cover for a boundary.
A bouncer, outside off, Lawrence ducks.
Good length ball, around off, pushed towards mid off.
Around off, pushed towards mid on.
Walks across the stumps and Henry fires an inswinging yorker. Dan Lawrence looks to adjust and flick but gets a leading edge towards point.
Outside off, slightly wider, left alone again. Over to Mr. Lawrence now...
The field is getting pushed back...
Outside off, swinging away, left alone.
Outside off, angling in. Anderson looks to push it away but the ball comes in, hits his thigh and the dribbles towards the slip cordon.
Down the leg side, a full toss, James Anderson gets across and then lets it pass.

Milestone man, James Anderson, walks in. He hung around at Lord's to help Rory Burns get to his century. Can he do something similar here, for Dan Lawrence? Time for shifting gears for the latter as well. Get the Big Bash mode on...

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! He was always looking like a cat on a hot tin roof and now, with the roof exploding, the cat falls. A length ball, outside off, once again Broad moves across and then back, looks to play at it and gets a thin outside edge. Easy catch for Tom Blundell, the keeper. Wait. Stop the press. Broad walks! Normally, he does not go until the umpire raises his finger. The world is changing then...
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Trent Boult

Commentary.Commentary: Full, going down the leg side, Stuart Broad shifts across to his off stump, then goes back and looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. Mild LBW appeals all around.
Fuller, around off, solidly defended.
Colin de Grandhomme is on the field. Not sure who has gone off.
On a good length, around off, punched towards mid on.
Fuller, around off, swinging in, played off the inner half of the bat towards mid on.

Angled down the leg side, Stuart Broad hops and tucks it towards fine leg for a single. Oh no says the umpire. Lifts his left leg and pats it, indicating that it is a leg bye. Not off the mark then...
Full, just around off, watchfully pushed towards gully.

Stuart Broad walks in now, at number 10, replacing Wood. After the latter's heroics, Broad would want to showcase his skills as well. He can bat for sure, can also use the long handle, but after being hit on the nose by a Varun Aaron bouncer in 2014, hasn't been the same batsman since.

OUT! BOWLED! See, it is not the short ball which will work always against the tail enders. Fuller lengths can work too, by keeping the ball straight. This is outside off, Mark Wood looks to drive hard but does not move his feet. Gets a thick inside edge which shatters the stumps. End of a terrific innings and a fine stand. The Edgbaston crowd gives Wood a fine support.
Another short ball, around middle and leg, Lawrence gets across and ducks.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards fine leg for a single.
A bouncer, down the leg side, swayed away from.

EDGED, FOUR! Throwing the bat at everything now. A length ball, outside off, Mark Wood slashes hard and gets a thick outside edge, which flies over point. Moves to 40 now. Did we say England would be thinking about Lawrence's century? Might have to rephrase.
Down the leg side, Wood misses his flick. This time Tom Blundell collects the ball with a dive to his left.

Lawrence into the act now. Full, outside off, Dan Lawrence pushes this down the ground. Beats mid off who starts to chase. It is Devon Conway. But Neil Wagner gets to it from mid on, tracking the ball down, diving and then pushing it back to Conway. Three runs taken. The stand moves to 61 and Lawrence moves to 71.
On a length, outside off, solidly defended. Well played, Mark Wood!
On a good length, outside off, shaping away, MW feels for it but misses.
Fuller, around off, pushed down to mid on.
Outside off, this time Mark slashes but misses. Wants to put bat on every ball!

FOUR! Ho ho ho! Mark seems to have the 'Wood' over New Zealand who seem rattled. He is having lot of fun and it has been all Wood so far. A short ball, outside off, Mark Wood backs away and then guides it over a leaping gully to the third man fence!

FOUR! BELLIGERENT! What an innings this is from Mark Wood. That is four boundaries on Day 2! Short, outside off, Wood swivels and instantaneously pulls it in front of square on the leg side! Moves to 32.
Down the leg side, Mark looks to tuck but misses. Tom Blundell dives to his left, but fumbles and concedes a bye. 50-RUN STAND IS UP!

FOUR! Nicely played, great timing as well. On a length, outside off, Wood just pushes this away from the body, not exactly hitting it from the middle of the bat. In fact, it has hit the bottom of the bat. Yet, it has raced away to the point fence.
Around off, moving away, left alone.
Change in the field and angle. Boult comes around the wicket, so fine leg moves finer.

TOP EDGE, FOUR! England are looking positive this morning. They are prepared to take everything on. A short ball, around middle, Mark Wood looks to hook. Gets a top edge which runs down very fine, bouncing just inside the ropes at fine leg.
There is good breeze around. It will definitely aid the swinging of the ball into the right hander, something which Boult is trying for, right now.
Outside off, no swing this time, angled away, left alone.
Fuller, around off, swinging in, watchfully defended.
Fuller, outside off, punched down the ground towards mid off.
Outside off, not exactly short, but shorter than good, DL looks to punch it through the covers but mistimes it towards cover.
Tempter, outside off, fuller in length, asking to drive, Dan lets it be.
Closer to the off stump, but outside the line. Lawrence knows where his stumps are and shoulders arms.
Fuller, outside off, watchfully left alone again.
On a length, outside off, Dan Lawrence takes his bat away from the line.
Matt Henry to bowl from the Birmingham End. 22-5-66-2 so far.
FOUR! HANDSOME! That has raced away. Overpitched, outside off, angling away, Mark Wood leans and drives it through the covers! Moves to 20 and the stand reads 41.
Around off, left alone.

GLOVED? Daryl Mitchell appeals from third slip but no one else is interested. A short ball, around off, angling away, Mark looks to sway away and tries to take his hand away. But the ball hits something and lobs to third slip where Mitchell takes the catch and appeals. Replays show that the ball hit Wood on his right hand.
A sharp short ball, around off, angling away, Wood leaps and then sways away from the line.
It is a different day today. The clouds are higher, the skies are brighter, there is lot of sunshine and then plenty of breeze. Conditions totally different from Thursday.
Around middle, on a length, watchfully defended.
A short ball, around middle, Dan Lawrence swivels and pulls it through fine leg for a single.

All set then, are we? The Edgbaston crowd certainly is. It gives a rauceous welcome and ovation to the overnight heroes - Dan Lawrence and Mark Wood. This stand is worth 36 and the pair would want to try and double it, if possible. Right then, the players are ready. Here comes Trent Boult with the first ball of Day 2 to Lawrence...

What about the Black Caps then? The age-old issue for many teams - dismissing the tail quickly. Might just want to keep Lawrence off strike and focus on the likes of Wood, Broad and Jimmy. Boult and Wagner are masters in getting rid of the tail but do not count out the spin of Ajaz Patel. The pitch showed signs of some turn on Day 1 and Friday might just make the ball spin more.

Dan Lawrence has stood tall and this morning session could well decide how strong England are in this Test. Their minimum target would be 300 but if Lawrence can go on past his century and the tail can wag a touch, especially the likes of Stuart Broad, we could even have 350 on the board.

Happy or disappointed? This is the argument I was having with my colleague after Stumps last evening. England 258/7, well not happy at all after winning the toss and that too, having had a wicketless opening session. 72/0 became 85/3 and the advantage was thrown away. But let's look at it from the other side. New Zealand had England at 169/5 with Rory Burns dismissed. Yet, from there, they have allowed the hosts to add 89 runs, picking up just 2 wickets. So they too, would be disappointed, won't they? Hence, it is fair to say, it was a balanced day of cricket.

What will the two sides now be looking for on Day 2? England will want to go past the 300 mark for that, Lawrence holds the key. New Zealand will not want that to happen. An exciting day awaits. Do join us for all the action. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Earlier in the day, after being asked to field, the away sides' bowlers were quite discipline in the first session but with no success. They had an excellent second where they dismissed the top order of England. The third session also initially belonged to them but they could not press home the advantage. Except for Mitchell all the others had a wicket atleast. They will be pretty pleased with their effort of Day 1, except for the last hour or so.

After picking two wickets in quick succession at the start of this session, the Kiwis had reduced the hosts to 175 for 6. However, Lawrence along with Stone counter-attacked, the two added some handy runs before Stone fell. Wood now is playing another decent knock along with Lawrence who is playing a gem.

A strong fight back from Lawrence along with the lower-order has taken England into a decent position. Can’t actually say which side will be the happier of the two but the Kiwis will be disappointed as they let the advantage slip away at one stage.
A touch fuller, on off, Wood defends it watchfully. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1.
A length ball, on leg, Wood flicks it to mid-wicket,

250 up! Fuller and on off, this is driven past mid off for a couple.

NOT OUT! It is off the flap of the pad! That is the reason Wood reviewed! This is on a length and around middle, it holds its line. Wood is squared up as he tries to block. It goes off something to the keeper. This time the finger is raised after an appeal. Wood signals the 'T' immediately and replays show that it is off the flap of the bat and Ball Tracker shows the ball is going over the stumps.

This time it is Mark Wood who goes for the review as he is caught behind. The Ultra Edge shows that there no spike as the ball passes the bat, as the replays confirm that the ball clips off the pads. And the Ball tracker shows that the ball is missing the wickets. The decision is over turned in the favour of Mark Wood. As England retain their review.
That is really well played! A yorker on middle, Wood jams it out.
A single! On middle, Wood looks to defend but this goes off the inner half through square leg for one.

New Zealand take the review, Matt Henry is very convinced here. Let's see what happens. The Ultra Edge shows there is spike as the ball passes the bat. The decision is unturned and Wood is still on the field. As New Zealand lose a review here.

NOT OUT! It is bat first! That was the only doubt, if it was bat first or pad and it is bat. Length and around off, Wood lunges to defend but he does so outside the line. It hits both bat and the pad. A huge appeal, turned down. Henry reviews but it shows that the Kiwis have lost their review.

FOUR! Whipped and whipped away for a boundary! Lawrence needed to hit that or he was a goner! This is full and on the pads, Lawrence shuffles across and whips it through mid-wicket. Races away. Lawrence is playing a gem of a knock here.

On middle, Lawrence works it to mid-wicket.

Lawrence almost played on there! This is short and on the body, Lawrence looks to pull but is a touch early in the shot. It hits the glove and misses the leg pole by just.

Good length again and on middle, kept out.
On middle, it is blocked.

On a length and around off, Wood looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge, lands short of the fielder at second slip. He makes a half stop. It goes behind for one.
Back of a length, it is kept out.

WOW! Thats a beauty! Good length ball, just outside the off pole. Wood looks to defend it but misses as the ball zips past the outside edge to the keeper.

A touch fuller, on off, Wood works it to mid off.

A full delivery on off, Wood defends it as the ball takes the inside edge and gets hit onto the pads.

Length and on middle. Blocked out.

Loopy ball, on off, Lawrence pushes it to mid off for a single and brings up his FIFTY! The crowd is showering him with applauds. This lad deserves it. He is keeping England in the game at the moment.

Stone decides to go for the review. The Ultra Edge confirm that there is no ball involved, and has hit the pads cleanly. The Ball Tracker shows THREE REDS  and Olly Stone is a goner. As  England lose a review.

DRINKS! This is a good fight back from the hosts! They were struggling at 175 for 6 but these two have steadied the ship somewhat. Can they continue or will New Zealand hit back after the break?

Good length and on off, blocked.

A slight misfield and a run! England are underway in this session on the first ball itself. Boult goes for the magic ball. An in swinging yorker, it shapes back in from outside off, Lawrence strokes it towards mid off for one.
We are back for the final session! The Kiwi players are out in the middle. Boult to begin. Lawrence and Burns to continue their innings.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

Pope and Burns then were building nicely before the former fell. Burns however, is battling it out hard but he needs someone to stick around. Can Lawrence do so? New Zealand on the other hand, will hope they can have a similar session like this one. Will we see a fightback from the hosts?
It was Henry who started off everything as he got Sibley in the very first over after Lunch. Root and Crawley then followed and England were in trouble then.
A really good session then for the Kiwis. They just gave away the 85 runs in the 27 overs and have managed to take 4 wickets.
FOUR! Played with elegance by Burns! Loopy ball, on leg, Rory Burns glances it to fine leg for a boundary as there is no man near it. This also brings up 150 for England. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 1.
Flatter on off, Lawrence punches this to cover for a single.
Loopy ball, outside off, Lawrence leaves it alone.
Floated on middle. nudged to mid-wicket.
Tossed up, full and on off, Dan Lawrence pushes it to mid off.
Loopy ball, on the pads, Lawrence flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
EDGY FOUR! A full delivery, on off, Burns looks to defend it but gets an outside edge as the ball goes past the diving fielder at gully for a boundary.
Another short ball, on middle, Burns decides to leave it at the last moment.
A length ball, outside off, left alone.
Effort ball! Wagner bends his back and serves a short ball, on the bodyline. Burns smartly sway away from the line of the delivery.
A length ball, down the leg side, Burns pulls it but gets the bottom edge as the ball goes to the left of Tom Blundell who makes brilliant stop.
Serves a length ball, on off, Burns nudges it to the leg side.
Loopy ball, on off, kept out.
1 run. Tossed up, on off, Rory Burns drives it to mid on for a single.
Floated on off, Burns nudges it to the leg side.
Loopy and full, on off, Burns pushes it to mid off.
Tossed up, on off, Burns camps back and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Loopy ball, on off, Dan Lawrence works it past point for a single.
FOUR! Put away! That is a half volley, a rare bad ball by Wagner and Burns puts it away. Full and outside off, it is driven through covers for a boundary.
Outside off again, this is guided to point.
Shorter and on off, blocked.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.
Back of a length and on middle, kept out.
Neil Wagner back into the attack now. His figures 11-4-29-1 so far.
FOUR! Pushed away! Shorter and on off, this is pushed through covers. A really good shot. First boundary for Lawrence and it brings out a big cheer from the crowd.
On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for two.
Watches this carefully and then lets it go outside off.
Big turn again! First real sign of the ball turning. This lands on off and then spins away. Lawrence is beaten as he tries to block.
Beaten! This is floated up on off, really nice and slow. It pitches and then turns away. Dan is beaten as he tries to drive.
On off, this is pushed to covers.
A single to end! On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for one. Lawrence is off the mark.
On off, kept out.

Was that an LBW? New Zealand go straight up for the review. The Ultra Edge shows us that there is no spike as the ball passes the bat. The Ball tracker confirms that the impact is outside off and the stumps weren't hitting. The NOT OUT decision stands.
NOT OUT! Impact is outside off! That seemed the case right from the time it hit the pad.
On middle, Burns looks to play it with a straight bat but it goes off the inner half through mid-wicket for one.
Once again, lovely shape away from the bowler. Outside off and moves away prodigiously. Left alone.
This is very full and on middle, Burns looks to jam it out but he gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Floats it up on off, this is pushed to cover. End a good over from Patel, a successful one.
On middle, kept out.
The new batsman to come in the  middle at No. 6 is Dan Lawrence.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Ajaz is into the attack and Ajaz gets Pope. Ollie will be gutted. He just put this away to the fence a couple of balls ago but now falls to the same ball. Not a good one. It is short and wide outside off again. Pope looks to cut again. This time he probably looked to get it a lot finer than he did the last time. It goes off the outside edge and it is taken by the keeper. Another start not converted by Pope and another partnership which was building nicely has been cut short.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: On off, this is pushed to cover.
Comes down the track but does not get to the pitch of it. Defended.
FOUR! Really nicely played! Yes, it is a bad ball but still has to be put away. This is short and outside off; this is cut through point for a boundary.
Sipn Now! Ajaz Patel is called into the action now. His figures 5-3-7-0 so far.
Almost! Fuller and tailing back in from middle, Pope looks to drive but this goes off the inside edge down to fine leg for one.
On middle, blocked.

Off the outer half! Good fielding job at the end. This is angled into middle, Pope looks to play it through the on side but it goes off the outer half and the man at point dives to his left and stops it.
From around the wicket to the right-hander. Length and on off, blocked.
Drags his length back a little, this is worked towards mid-wicket for one.
Beautiful away movement on this one. Fuller and on off, it is driven to mid off.
This one does not come out that well! It is well wide outside off, left alone.
Slightly fuller and on middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for one.
Mitchell is getting some nice shape. This time into the batter but the line is outside off. Left alone.
A gentle delivery on middle, it is driven back to the bowler.
Fuller and on off, this is driven but to mid off.
Loose from Burns! Shorter and outside off, Rory goes after it away from his body. He slashes but misses.
A length ball, down the leg side, Pope has a go at it but misses. 5 of the over. Boult has been good today but is yet to get a wicket under his name.
A full ball, on leg, Burns removes his front leg and clips it deep square leg for a single.
A length ball, on off, blocked solidly.
Good length ball, outside off, Burns shoulders arms to it.
FOUR! SHORT AND PUNISHED! Back of a length delivery on off, Burns pulls this one through mid-wicket for a boundary.
A length ball, on off, Burns gets behind the line of the ball and keeps it out.
On a length ball, outside off, Ollie Pope lets it go to the keeper.
Full ball, on leg, Pope flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
A length ball, on off, pushed to mid on.
Serves a fullish delivery now, on off, Pope is forced to play this one as he pushes it to cover.
Another length ball, outside off, Pope leaves it alone.
On a length, outside off, Pope shoulders arms to it.
A length ball, on off Burns defends it watchfully.
A full ball, outside off, Pope punches it to cover but cannot find the gap. As the batters take a single.
Good length ball, on off, Pope defends it onto the pitch.
A short ball, around off, the ball takes off as it hits the deck. Pope sways away from the line of the delivery.
Good length ball, on off, Pope pushes it to cover.
Fires in a length ball, on off, Pope keeps it out.
Another length ball, on off, Burns blocks it to cover.
A length ball, on off, Pope pushes it to mid off for a single.
A length ball, way outside off, Pope shoulders arms to it.
A touch short, on off, Burns pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.

A length ball, on off, Burns punches it through cover for a couple. That brings up his half-century. What a solid knock form Burns. England needed this right now and would hope that he sticks out for long.
Serves a good length ball, outside off, Burns lets it go to the keeper.

DRINKS!! A really good hour for the visitors. They came out all guns blazing after Lunch and took three wickets in quick succession, pushing England onto the back foot. However, Pope and Burns have started well but they need to go on. England will hope the two can build a good stand. New Zealand on the other hand, will hope they can keep picking wickets at regular intervals.
A dot to end then! On off, it is pushed to mid off.
Gets this one to tail back in a little from around off, blocked.
On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
This one is angled away from outside off, left alone.
Another one on a length and around off, this is pushed to covers again.
Length and on off, Pope gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
Changes from both the ends now as Trent Boult comes into the attack. His figures 9-2-18-0 so far.
On off, kept out.
Ohhhh! Short and down the leg side, Burns looks to pull but misses. Had he got a glove to that, he would have been disgusted.
Good length and on off, this is pushed to covers.
Outside off, left alone.
The inswinger this time but the line is way down the leg side. The keeper does really well to dive to his right and stop it.
Daryl Mitchell comes into the attack now. His figures 3-0-11-0 so far.
Good length and on off, Burns guides it to gully.
Another length ball, outside off, left alone.
Way outside off, left alone.
A touch fuller, on leg, Pope flicks it past mid on. The fielder makes an excellent stop before the boundary line. But the batters run four this time, no problem if they can't get a boundary.
Slightly fuller and on leg, Pope flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
No run. Length and on off, pushed to cover.
A length ball, way outside off, Pope shoulders arms to it..
A short ball to end the over! Burns sits under this one.

FOUR! That is a fabulous shot by Burns! Which also brings up 100 for England. A length ball, outside off, Burns slashes it through the cover region for a boundary. That would relieve some pressure from Burns.
A length ball, on off, Burns blocks it to cover.
Good length ball, down the leg side, Burns looks to flick it but misses.
Back of a length delivery, on middle, Burns ducks under this one.
On a length outside off, Burns pushes it to cover.
A full length delivery on off, Pope blocks it to cover.
Serves a good length ball, outside off, Pope shoulders arms to it.
A full ball, on middle, Burns clips it to mid-wicket and takes a quick single. Good running here.
A length ball, on off, kept out.
A touch fuller, outside off, Burns prods and drives it to mid off.
Good length ball, outside off, Burns has no stroke to offer.
A length ball, outside off, Pope leaves it alone.
Good length ball, way outside off, Pope shoulders arms to it.
A length ball, outside off, Burns drives it with soft hand past mid off. The chasing fielder makes a great stop in the deep. The batter come back for three comfortably.
Fullish delivery, around off, kept out solidly.
A length ball, on off, Pope drives it down the ground past mid on for three.
Good length ball, outside off, left alone.
LEG BYE! A loud appeal for LBW but the umpire is unmoved. A full ball, on the pads, Pope looks to flicks it but misses and gets hit on the pads. The batters sneak a run. Leg bye given.
On a length, on the pads, Pope nudges it to mid-wicket.
A touch fuller, on off, Pope defends watchfully.
Serves a length ball, outside off, Pope punches it with the bottom of the bat to mid off.
A length ball, outside off, Pope pushes it to point.
A good length ball, on the fourth stump line. Pope shoulders arms to it.
A back of a length delivery, on middle, Burns decides to duck again. Just a single of the over.
A touch short, on off, Burns defends it to the off side.
Another short ball, on middle, Burns sits under this one.
Short ball, on the bodyline, Burns looks to pull it but misses as the ball goes through to the keeper.
A length ball, on the pads, Burns tucks it to the leg side.
A length ball, on the pads, Pope glances it to fine leg for a single.
A length ball, on off, Burns works it to cover. A tight over from Neil Wagner.
Full ball, on middle and leg, Burns pushes it to mid on.
Serves a good length ball, outside off, Burns goes back to his patient side and leaves it alone.
FOUR! Well played shot by Burns! Fuller outside off, Burns slashes it through backward point for a boundary,
A touch fuller, on off, Burns defends it solidly.
Good length ball, outside off, Burns leaves it for the keeper.
A length ball, outside off, left alone.
Next batsman coming in at No. 5 is Ollie Pope

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! OH MY GOD! The consistent balling of good line and length is paying off Matt Henry now. He gets his second for the day and he gets the main man this time as Joe Root has to depart early. Good length ball, outside off, Root looks to defend but gets a thin outside edge as the ball gets carried to Tom Blundell behind the wickets who takes an easy catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Matt Henry

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! EDGY FOUR! A length ball, outside off, Root looks to push it to the off side but gets an outside edge as the ball goes through the gap between slip and gully for a bounday.
A full delivery on middle, Joe Root blocks it back to the bowler.
Good length on off, Root punches it off his back foot to point.
Fires in a length ball, on off, Root pushes it to the off side.
Another length ball, outside off, Root has no bat to offer.
On a length, outside off, left alone.
A length ball, around off, Burns pushes it out.
Fires in a good length ball, outside off, Burns shoulders arms to it.
Serves a fullish delivery, on off, Burns blocks it watchfully.
Good length ball, on off, kept out.

FOUR BYES! Root was beaten but the keeper couldn't keep the ball in his mitts as it rushes through for a boundary at fine leg.Good length ball, outside off, Joe Root looks to defend as the ball sways away and gets beaten but get the freebie.
Good length ball, just outside the off pole. Root lets it go to the keeper.

NO BALL! A length ball on off, this time Burns times his drive well and gets it past mid off, but the ball does not have enough legs to reach the boundary, as the fielder mops up. The batters pick three. Overstepped, No ball given.
Good length ball, on off, Burns keeps it out.
A full delivery on the middle and off, Burns blocks solidly.
Another length ball, on off, Burns blocks it watchfully.
A length ball, outside off, left alone
The batsman coming in at No. 4 is Joe Root.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! The Kiwis have two in two overs. Whatever they have had for Lunch is surely working. Crawley bags a duck and his poor run continues. Wagner sets him up brilliantly. He got the last two balls to come back in. This one is angled away from off. Crawley has a tentative poke at it. He is worried about the ball coming back in. This one does not and it goes off the outside edge. It is taken by Mitchell at second slip. England in a spot of bother.
Commentary.Howout: c Daryl Mitchell b Neil Wagner

Commentary.Commentary: Almost! That is a lovely delivery by Wagner. Exactly what he has been wanting to do. He is trying to get the ball back in from outside off but he has been a little too wide. This time gets it back in from a little more closer to the off pole. Crawley initially looks to leave it but then sees it coming back in, tries to block but is beaten for pace. He's fortunate it just goes past the off pole.
And again, outside off, left alone.
Quite wide outside off, Crawley need not play at those so early in his innings.
Sticks with the fuller length. This time Burns strokes it towards mid off and gets to the other end.
Outside off, on the fuller side. Some away movement for Wagner as well. Left alone.
The next batsman coming in at No. 3 is Zak Crawley. While, Neil Wagner comes into the attack from the other end.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! There is the wicket New Zealand wanted and they draw first blood immediately after Lunch. Perfect start for them and that is a lovely delivery from Henry. He lands it on off and on a length which means Sibley has to play at it. The ball moves away just enough to kiss the outside edge and go into the hands of the keeper. A gritty knock from Sibley comes to an end. He falls after getting off to get another start. Can the Kiwis build on this?
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Matt Henry

Commentary.Commentary: Just outside off, left alone.

STREAKY FOUR! Better from Henry. Lands this closer to the off pole and gets it to shape away. Sibley pushes at it, this one goes off the outside edge but between gully and third slip for a boundary. Sibley too is off the mark in this session.
First sign of swing for Henry in this session but the line is well wide outside off. Left alone.

That does not bounce at all, at least not as much as Sibley thought it would. Length and just outside off, shorter than a length actually. Sibley drops his hands and tries to leave it alone but the ball does not bounce a lot, it hits the glove and to his luck, goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Henry starts with a length ball, around the hips, Burns glances it to fine leg for a single. First run of this session and it does not take long to score it.

We are all set to resume! The Kiwis make their way out for the afternoon session and so do the English openers, Rory Burns and Dominic Sibely to resume their innings. Matt Henry to begin. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

Nothing ill can be said about the Kiwi bowling though. They bowled well, hit the right areas, kept things tight, swung the ball, moved it off the seam, but have not been able to enforce many mistakes or get the edge. The sun was out for a brief moment during the first session but it has mostly been overcast throughout. The openers have done all the hard work. It is time now to cash in. New Zealand, on the other hand, will aim for a good start after Lunch as a break generally disrupts concentration. Join us back at 1.40 pm local (1240 GMT).

Wonderful opening session for England. Something which they have longed to see consistently in the last few years - both openers walking back unscathed. Too many times they have been 20/3 or 30/2 but this has been a solid beginning. Dominic Sibley has looked a bit scratchy but in between, has played some wonderful shots as well. Rory Burns has looked compact and assuring.
Outside off, pushed towards mid off. LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Ooohhh.. what as that? Swinger? Seam up, swinging back into the right hander, yes, swinging back in, pitches and then skids through. Sibley somehow blocks it out in a hurry, crouching as an after effect.
Flatter around off, solidly blocked out.
Fuller, around middle, whipped straight to short mid-wicket.
Short, outside off, punched straight to cover. 'YEAH! WAIT, WAIT, WAIT!' is the call.
Full, around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Around off, squirted through point for a couple.
On a length, outside off, Burns walks down the track and pushes it towards cover.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.

Ooohh... nearly did him in there. Trent Boult slips in a low full toss on the leg stump. Rory Burns looks to flick but is a second late. The ball almost goes past the bat but somehow, takes the leading edge and goes to cover.
Around off, on a length, shaping away, Rory Burns feels for it but misses.
Fuller, around middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Fuller, around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Fuller, around middle, blocked towards the bowler.
Looped up, around off, Dominic Sibley lunges and blocks.
Fired in outside off, left alone.
Comes down the track this time, does Burns, gets a bit adventurous, reaches out and pushes the ball wide of mid off, to his right, for a single. Moves to 30.
Full, around off, watchfully defended.
First real aggressive shot. Short, around off, Burns swivels and pulls it all along the ground to fine leg for a run.
Around middle, nudged towards mid on.
Around off, pushed towards point.
Landed around off, solidly defended.
Fuller, around off, defended solidly.
Short outside off, left alone.
Fuller, around middle, pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Nice shot. Dominic Sibley is growing in confidence. Short, outside off, Sibley rocks back and punches it through the covers.
Short, outside off, cut straight to point.

NOT OUT. Well in, is Burns. Full, around middle, Rory Burns pushes it towards mid on and sets off for a quick single. Neil Wagner gets to the ball and fires a throw at the stumps at the bowler's end. There is barely any appeal but the on-field umpire takes it upstairs. One replay is good enough to make the decision. David Lloyd on air informs us that even if the on-field umpire feels the batsman is safe, it is his duty to refer it upstairs for a second look, as per the instructions.
Having a look... We have an appeal for a run out which is referred upstairs but no one looks remotely interested. Yeah, the reason is Burns well being in.
Fuller, around off, watchfully defended.
Short, outside off, cut through point for a single.
The cut again, this time to the left of the gully fielder. This time he dives and stops it.
FOUR! Short, outside off, Rory Burns rocks back and cuts it to the right of gully and finds the third man fence.
Short ball. Burns ducks under it.
Around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Fuller, around off, swinging away, watchfully pushed towards cover.
On a length, outside off, pushed towards point.
Outside off, left alone.
Shorter, around off, Sibley looks to punch but gets a bottom edge back to the bowler.
Fuller, around off, Dominic Sibley looks to push but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat towards square leg.
Fuller, around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Ajaz gives this one air on off. Sibley blocks it.
Full, around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full, outside off, pushed towards point.
Outside off, swinging away, left alone.
Fuller, down the leg side, with a bit of swing too, clipped towards long leg for a single.
Fuller, around off, pushed hurriedly towards mid off, like a half drive.
Similar ball, angling away, let through again.
On a good length, around off, angling away, left alone.
Hmmm... we have a left-armer from the other end as well. Trent Boult returns into the attack as the floodlights get switched on as well. 5-2-10-0 so far.
Around off, well blocked out. Nice start from Ajaz.
Faster, around middle, worked towards guess who - FSL.
Fuller, around middle, nudged towards short leg once more.
Quicker through the air, outside off, watchfully defended.
Fuller, around middle, worked towards short leg again.
Around off, a touch short, worked towards short leg.
We are going to see some spin now. Left-arm orthodox, Ajaz Patel, replaces Neil Wagner. Interestingly, this end has featured all left-armers so far.
FOUR! Easy pickings for Dominic Sibley. A length ball, down the leg side, Sibley just works it through mid-wicket. 50-STAND IS UP!
That came out of nowhere. On a length, outside off, suddenly rears up, Dominic is watchful and hops with the ball, swaying away from the line.
Around middle, nudged to the leg side.
Full, down the leg side, clipped towards fine leg for a single.
On a length, around off, coming back in, defended to the off side.
Full, around off, swinging away, pushed down the ground through mid on for a single.
On a length outside off, left alone.
Outside off, asking Burns to drive but he refuses to play at that.
Around middle, Dominic Sibley tucks it to the leg side and calls for a tight single. Ajaz Patel gets to his left from square leg but while picking up the ball, fumbles. Single is easily completed.
A short ball, around off, Sibley ducks.
Outside off, punched through the covers to get three and move into the 20s.

EDGED, FOUR! Not sure Burns was aiming it through that region. Full, around leg, swinging away, Rory Burns looks to flick but the away swing induces a leading edge. The ball goes between third slip and gully and skipper Tom Latham gives it a chase from gully, gets to the ball, tries to push it back but fails. He then lands very hard on the advertising board and injures his right elbow. Winces in pain. This stand moves to 42.
Outside off, on a length, moving away, left alone.
Very full, outside off, swinging away, dug out back to the bowler.
On a length, outside off, left alone.

Around middle, nudged through mid-wicket. Neil Wagner gives it a chase and whole-heartedly slides to his left, pushes the ball back and it is collected by Ajaz Patel who was tracking it from the inner circle. Three runs are taken.
Swing, but down the leg side. Rory Burns misses his flick.
On a length, outside off, angling very wide, away from the batter, left alone.
Outside off, on a length, shaping away, left alone.

FOUR! GORGEOUS! Better application from Sibley this time. Very full again from Wagner, this time Dominic makes sure his footwork is neat. Leans to the pitch of the ball, closes the the face of the bat and drives it through the covers.
Around off, solidly kept out.
Fuller, around off, pushed towards mid off.
On a length, outside off, left alone.

IN THE AIR... JUST WIDE OF POINT... FOUR! Neil Wagner almost gets the breakthrough. Fuller, wider, outside off, Dominic Sibley gets sucked into that and plays a loose drive. The ball flies in the air but eludes the diving fielder at point. to his right. Trickles into the fence behind. The stand moves to 31.
That is a beauty. Pitching on a length outside leg and then nipping away past Burns as he looked to defend.
On a length, around off, moving away, Rory Burns is squared up as he looks to defend. Gets an outside edge but because he played it with soft ands, the edge does not carry to gully.
Fuller, around middle, driven towards mid on.
Very full, outside off, dug out towards cover.
On a good length, around leg, rearing away, pushed back down the track a touch awkwardly.
Full, around middle, some swing, clipped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Change of bowling at the Birmingham end. Daryl Mitchell to bowl now.
This one swings back in. It is on off, Sibley defends it with a straight bat. Maiden to begin the second hour of the first session.
This time Wagner comes close to the stumps and bowls it full on off. Sibley keeps it out.
Good length ball outside off, Sibley is not interested in that.
Full outside off, Sibley lets it carry to the keeper.
This is well wide of the stumps. Wagner wants Sibley to go for the drive but Dom is not too keen on it.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
DRINKS BREAK.
Fuller, around off, angling away, shouldered arms to.
Around middle, tucked to the leg side.
Around off, solidly defended.
Beauty! On a length, around off, Rory Burns looks to drive but misses.
Outside off, driven on the up through the covers for a couple.
Fuller, around off, pushed towards cover.
Around off, well defended.
Very full, around off, swinging in, pushed towards mid on.
Fuller, around off, Sibley is squared up but at the last moment, manages to get his bat down in time to push the ball towards cover.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Outside off, on a length, left alone.

It was bright and sunny this morning but it has gone overcast now. There is no rain forecast but the light has dipped tremendously. Good conditions for swing bowlers. Meanwhile, Daryl Mitchell is warming up.
Full, around off, Dominic Sibley pushes it towards gully.
On a good length, around off, pushed towards point.
Outside off, angling away, left alone.
Fuller, around off, Rory Burns looks to push it through the off side but the ball straightens and goes off the inner half of the bat towards mid on.
On a length, outside off, seaming away, let through.
A bit too straight this time, clipped towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Somebody is off the field. Because Tim Southee is on and is fielding at third slip.
On a length outside off, Dominic Sibley feels for it but misses.
Terrific delivery to end the over.  On a length, outside off, Rory Burns feels for it but the ball kicks off after landing and beats the outside edge. Neil Wagner smiles.
Very full, outside off, watchfully pushed out.
Full and wide outside off, let through again.

Ha ha ha... Michael Holding and his jokes. Holding recounts the year 1976 when he visited Leeds and actually saw people SITTING on the sightscreen but no batsman had an issue with that. Feels irritated that batsmen these days hold up play at the slightest moment.
More swing, outside off, let through again.
Full and wide outside off, swinging away, shouldered arms to.
Around middle and leg, tucked towards fine leg for a single. Sibley moves into double figures.
First bowling change of the Test. Neil Wagner into the attack now.
On the pads, turned towards deep square leg for a couple. The stand moves to 21.
Fuller, around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Now he pushes this to the off side.
Around off, worked to the leg side.
Around off, solidly defended.
Full, around middle, pushed down the ground. Neil Wagner gives it a chase and stops it near the ropes with a slide. Three runs taken.
Outside off, well wide, left alone.

There is that nip backer. From outside off, Rory Burns looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. Boult appeals for LBW, extends it as well, but umpire Richard Kettleborough is not interested. Perhaps a bit too high. UltraEdge detects an inside edge.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full, around middle, worked towards short mid-wicket.

This is in that corridor of uncertainty, or the avenue of apprehension, outside off, on a length, batsmen have confusion whether to play or leave, so does Burns, plays it late and gets beaten due to the late movement.
Full, outside off, pushed to the off side.
Outside off, nips back in a long way, Sibley shoulders arms and the ball just misses the off stump!
Full, outside off, moving away, Dominic Sibley feels for it but misses.
Around middle, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Outside off, rises off a length, Sibley fends it off towards leg gully.
On a good length around off, watchfully blocked out.
Outside off, left alone.
Full, outside off, left alone.
A bouncer, down the leg side. swayed under.
On a length, outside off, pushed towards point.
Three awayswingers outside off and Burns leaves it for the third time in a row.
A carbon copy of the previous delivery.
An awayswinger outside off, Burns watches it sail into the keeper's mitts.

Nips back off the seam! A back of a length delivery, outside off, nips back in sharply, as Dominic Sibley raises his blade and does not want anything to do with the ball this time. End of a good over for the Kiwis.
Slightly behind the good length and on off, Sibley blocks it nicely.
Another solid defense offered by Sibley.
Full, around off, solidly blocked out.
That's a good ball. 83 mph bouncer, around off, Dominic Sibley sways and lets it pass.
Full, outside off, asking to be driven, not answered. Left alone.
Fuller, a bit straighter, clipped through mid-wicket. Devon Conway gives it a chase and the batsmen run hard to cross each other thrice.
On middle and leg, tucked towards short mid-wicket.
Full, outside off, pushed wide of mid off. Ajaz Patel gives it a chase and keeps the batsmen to a run.
A touch short, on the hips, turned away, just past a fine square leg, to his right, for a single. Interesting field placement.
Fuller, outside off, this time Dominic Sibley lunges and pushes it towards cover.
Outside off, swinging away, left alone.
Down the leg side, Rory misses his tuck and the ball goes off his thigh pads towards fine leg. Two leg byes taken.
On a length, around middle, watchfully patted back.
Around off, Burns defends it towards short mid-wicket.
Full, around off, watchfully pushed towards cover.
Around middle and leg, straightening a touch, Rory Burns  looks to work it to the leg side but misses and is hit on the pads.
Very full, around middle, watchfully pushed towrads mid off.
Very full, but down the leg side, flicked through square leg for a single.
Around off, nipping back in sharply, Rory misses his tuck and is hit on the pads.
Outside off, pushed towards gully.
Fuller, around off, pushed towards gully.
Outside off, let through to the keeper.
Around off, Burns looks to defend but gets a bit of an outside edge towards gully.
Full, around off, well defended.
Very full, outside off, dug out back to the bowler.
Around off, on a length, let through.
WIDE! Very rare, very rare in a Test match. But this one was very very wide. Full, outside off, almost swings way past the pitch.  Tom Blundell does well to take it with a dive to his right.
Very full, around off, swinging in, flicked through mid-wicket. Two fielders give it a chase and Sibley is on the board with a couple.
2 runs.
Outside off, pushed towards gully.
Full, around off, watchfully defended.
Matt Henry to share the new ball with Boult.

FOUR! Through that gap between slips and gully! He always manages to exploit that. doesn't he? Length ball, outside off, shaping away, Burns plays at it with soft hands, gets a bit of an outsid eedge but it escapes along the ground, through that gap, to the third man fence. England are underway.
Outside off, left alone again.
Around off, pushed towards cover.
Play and a miss! On a length, just outside off, Rory Burns feels for it but misses, as it moves away a touch.
Slightly wider than the previous one, easier leave outside off.
What a start. Full, just outside off, swinging away. Should it be played? Should it be left? Burns does the latter.

All ready? You bet! The second Test is all set to get underway! The English openers, Rory Burns and Dominic Sibley, have come to the crease. The returning man, Trent Boult, is all set to take the new ball. Burns to face. Three slips and a gully. Let's play!

England (Playing XI) - Rory Burns, Dominic Sibley, Zak Crawley, Joe Root (C), Ollie Pope, Dan Lawrence, James Bracey (WK), Olly Stone (IN FOR OLLIE ROBINSON), Mark Wood, Stuart Broad and James Anderson. Just the one change here...

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham (C), Devon Conway, Will Young (IN FOR KANE WILLIAMSON), Ross Taylor, Henry Nicholls, Tom Blundell (WK) (IN FOR BJ WATLING), Daryl Mitchell (IN FOR COLIN DE GRANDHOMME), Neil Wagner, Matt Henry (IN FOR MITCHELL SANTNER), Ajaz Patel (IN FOR TIM SOUTHEE) and Trent Boult (IN FOR KYLE JAMIESON). Wow. That's 6 changes to the previous XI!
TOSS - The flip of the coin is done. Tom Latham has called incorrectly and ENGLAND WILL BAT FIRST.

Jimmy the man. Another big day for the Lancashire great. This will be the 162nd Test match for James Anderson, the most by any player to have represented England in Test cricket. And Jimmy is not done yet. He will go past Sir Alastair Cook and would want to produce a special performance.

MORE BREAKING NEWS - Well, seems like injuries are biting New Zealand one after the other. First, Mitchell Santner. Then, Kane Williamson. ​​​​​Now, BJ Watling. This would have been his penultimate Test but unfortunately for him, his sore back has troubled him. So he misses out from this game. Tom Blundell will be the man with the gloves for this game.

The first Test was a draw. Time for the second one now. The first one was a batting paradise. The second might be a deck for the spinners. No Robinson for England. No Williamson and Santner for New Zealand. Who holds the edge? We shall find out in the span of say, 5 days? Hello and a warm welcome to the second Test between England and New Zealand at Edgbaston.
